successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the whole sultanate: the Dutch annexed Aceh as 'Gouvernement of Atjeh and Dependencies', with wider control only after 1908; Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies shape includes Aceh from 1914

ledger.x: c. 1514: Ali Mughayat Syah founds the Aceh Sultanate at Bandar Aceh Darussalam and the Pedir vassalage ends. Reign list 'c. 1514-1530'; infobox 'Vassal of the Pedir Kingdom (1497-1514)'; 'The sultanate was founded by Ali Mughayat Syah' (the infobox also says 'Founded 1480', not supported by the text).
1522: Ali Mughayat Syah takes Pedir.
1523: Aceh invades Pasai, a Portuguese ally.
1524: Aceh annexes Samudera Pasai.
1524: the Portuguese garrison leaves Pasai and the fighting ends.

c. 1526: Aceh extends over the highlands south-east of its core. Cliopatria's shape grows by 33 cells here; the page says only that Ali Mughayat Syah 'began campaigns to extend his control over northern Sumatra and the Indonesia in 1520' and that his conquests 'included Deli, Pedir, and Pasai, and he attacked Aru'…
1539: Alauddin al-Kahar goes to war with the Batak south of Aceh.

c. 1572: Aceh's homeland reaches its full extent in the uplands and the north-east coast. Cliopatria's 1572 step (+52 cells, 60,219 km2) follows the accession of Ali Ri'ayat Syah I (1571); no page opened dates the conquest. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the Alauddin al-Kahar page ends with his death on 28 September 1571 and…

c. 1609: Aceh governors take the west coast of Sumatra. 'forced to recognise the sovereignty of the Sultanate of Aceh' and accepted Aceh-appointed governors for the west coast, in the 'early 17th century' (no year); 1609 is Cliopatria's step, two years after Iskandar Muda's accession. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the…

c. 1609: the Minangkabau kingdom of Pagaruyung recognises Aceh's sovereignty. The page gives 'early 17th century' and no year; ended 1666 ('Aceh's influence on Pagaruyung then weakened'). Re-checked 2026-10-19: no page gives a year.
1612: Iskandar Muda conquers Deli.
1613: Iskandar Muda conquers Aru.
1613: Johor is taken.
1613: Johor expels the Acehnese garrison the same year.
1617: Iskandar Muda conquers Pahang.
1617: the page records the conquest and the sultan's removal, nothing about holding Pahang; closed the same year as a raid.
1619: Aceh takes Kedah.
1619: the page records a sack, not a lasting occupation; closed the same year.
1620: Perak is captured.
1623: Iskandar Muda sacks Johor a second time.
1623: the sack ends the same year; the page gives no garrison or occupation (bridged).
1624: Iskandar Muda takes Nias.
1629: after the failed attack on Malacca, Perak defects to the Portuguese.
1641: after Iskandar Thani (d.
1666: the VOC expels Aceh from the west coast of Sumatra.
1666: Pagaruyung escapes Aceh.
1669: Deli falls away.
1873: the Dutch attack Aceh.
January 1874: the Dutch take the dalam and Sultan Mahmud Syah abandons Banda Aceh.
1878: the court moves to Indrapuri (Aceh Sultanate page: Pagar Ayer 1875-1878, Indrapuri 1878-1879).
1879: the court moves to Keumala (Keumala 1879-1898).
1898: the court leaves Keumala for Kuta Sawang and then Batee Illiek-Samalanga as van Heutsz, 'proclaimed governor of Aceh' in 1898, presses in (Aceh War page).
1901: the court moves to Loyang Sekam-Laut (1901-1903).
1904: the war ends in Dutch victory.
1904: Aceh passes to the Dutch East Indies.
1904: the Aceh Sultanate ends.

wars.name: Acehnese-Portuguese conflicts
wars.outcome: Aceh took Pedir (1522) and Pasai (1523-1524) from the Portuguese orbit, besieged Malacca repeatedly (1537, 1547, 1568, 1573, 1575, 1582, 1615, 1629) without taking it, and its great 1629 attack failed.

wars.name: Iskandar Muda's conquests in Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula
wars.outcome: Deli (1612), Aru and Johor (1613), Pahang (1617), Kedah (1619/20), Perak (1620) and Nias (1624/5); the peninsular conquests were sacks and captive-taking that did not outlast 1629.

wars.name: Expulsion of Aceh from the west coast of Sumatra
wars.outcome: The VOC arrived at Padang in 1663; the Minang revolted against the Aceh governors around 1665; in 1666 the VOC drove Aceh from the coast.

wars.name: Aceh War
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: the capital fell in January 1874, the Dutch withdrew behind a fortified line around Banda Aceh in 1884, van Heutsz and Colijn conquered most of Aceh from 1898, the sultan capitulated in 1903 and the sultanate surrendered in 1904.

certainty.note: The Sumatran uplands, the east-coast lands and the west-coast governors' reach are approximate; no treaty fixes any frontier.
The homeland is a coast-and-valley realm of semi-autonomous uleebalang; the Dutch and British treaties (1871) fixed spheres, not lines.
